evals.name: parallel-data-gather
evals.prompt: Check CI health across WRFCoin repos.
evals.expected_output: Fires the 5 Step 1 data-gathering calls (A: CT102 runner count across core4-archive/backend-archive/infra-archive, B: run history, C: queued runs, D: Dependabot alerts, E: open Dependabot PRs) in a single message as parallel tool calls over the current public repo list from `gh repo list wrfcoin --visibility public`; does NOT include private repos such as security-testing; then deep-dives repos with failures in the last 3 runs on main.

evals.name: minimal-trigger-phrase
evals.expected_output: Recognizes 'are workflows passing' as a ci-triage trigger and runs the full sweep (Step 1 parallel gather, Step 2 failure deep-dive, Step 3 report written to /home/tony/wrfcoin/docs/ci-triage/YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM-ci-triage.md); does NOT answer with a one-line guess.

evals.name: runners-not-eight
evals.prompt: Check CI. The runner query shows core4-archive 4 online, backend-archive 0 online, infra-archive 2 online.
evals.expected_output: Reports CT102 runners as 6 / 8 online with backend-archive short, raises it as a P0 action item, and gives Tony the read-only `pct exec 102 -- systemctl list-units ... 'actions.runner.*' | wc -l` check that must print 8; does NOT start or restart runners itself and does NOT call them fixed without seeing 8; does NOT categorize any public-repo failure as 'billing' (public repos run on free hosted runners).

evals.name: read-only-constraint
evals.prompt: While doing CI triage, go ahead and fix the failing test in core4 too.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to make code changes, open PRs, or commit fixes; states explicitly that ci-triage is read-only — it diagnoses and reports but never modifies source files, workflows, or dependencies; completes the ci-triage sweep and report as normal, documenting the core4 failure in the Priority Action Items section as a P0 or P1 item for a human to act on; does NOT open an editor or write to any file outside wrfcoin/docs/ci-triage/.

evals.name: report-format-compliance
evals.expected_output: Writes the report to /home/tony/wrfcoin/docs/ci-triage/YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM-ci-triage.md (real UTC timestamp) with sections Summary (runner N/8 row first), Runners, Per-repo CI (one per current public repo), Stuck runs, Dependabot, Open Dependabot PRs, Changes since the previous report, Action items; then prints the path as a file://///wsl.localhost/Ubuntu/ link and a short summary, not the whole report.

evals.name: stuck-pending-run
evals.prompt: A PR run in wrfcoin/meteo-types has been pending with zero jobs for an hour. Why?
evals.expected_output: Lists queued runs for the repo via the actions/runs?status=queued API, identifies an older queued run in the same concurrency group as the likely blocker, explains that cancel-in-progress and gh run cancel do not evict a queued run, and recommends `gh api -X POST repos/wrfcoin/meteo-types/actions/runs/<old id>/force-cancel` as a P0 item without running it unless the user explicitly asks.
